issues.title: Discrete coercivity dissipation scaling
issues.failure_explanation: The weighted velocity norm is Delta v times the unweighted sum, and the dissipation identity contains (1/Delta v) times the sum of squared differences. Thus the local Dirichlet form compatible with the stated eigenvalue lambda_N is (1/Delta v) times that sum. With the old Delta v^{-2} definition, the proof omits the compensating Delta v factors, so its displayed Poincare step and final coercivity estimate do not follow as written.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition prop:coercivity, and therefore the coercivity input used by thm:main_AP, is unsupported until the grid-weight scaling is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the local energy definition by [D(u)]_p := Δv^{-1} Σ_{q=1}^{N_v-1}(u_{p,q+1}-u_{p,q})² and carry this weighted energy through the dissipation lower bound. The stated discrete Poincaré eigenvalue λ_N then yields the existing γ_h, leaving prop:coercivity and its use in thm:main_AP unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof mixes an unweighted Δv^{-2} sum with the Δv-weighted velocity norm, so its quantitative inference requires a normalization check rather than merely an ignorable transcriptional reading. The repair is nevertheless short and routine, requires no new lemma, and preserves the exact coercivity and downstream AP guarantees.

issues.title: Undefined Maxwellian extrema in discrete coercivity
issues.failure_explanation: The complete old source does not define the unsuperscripted M_min and M_max before they enter gamma_h. Their required roles are different: M_min must lower-bound half-grid flux coefficients, while M_max must upper-bound cell-centered Maxwellian values. Without specifying those grids and extrema, gamma_h is not a source-defined constant and the proposition's quantitative statement is incomplete.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity constant in prop:coercivity, and hence the gap and amplification factor used by thm:main_AP, are not well-defined from the old source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the constants in prop:coercivity explicitly by M_min := min_{p,q} M_{p,q+1/2} and M_max := max_{p,q} M_{p,q}, and use the corresponding time-level extrema when γ_h is invoked in thm:main_AP. This makes the coercivity constant and its downstream occurrence well-defined without changing either estimate.
issues.why_classification: The two undefined symbols must be assigned extrema on different grids, so a genuine mathematical specification is needed rather than a uniquely determined token correction. Those definitions are directly dictated by the existing proof, are entirely local, and cause no weakening, new argument, or change of rate or scope.

issues.title: Mean-norm factor in discrete coercivity
issues.failure_explanation: The old displayed estimate gives a bound for the scalar bar u squared containing L_v M_max. Since the constant velocity vector has squared norm L_v times bar u squared, that estimate would yield another factor of L_v and does not imply the next displayed factor (1+sqrt(L_v M_max)) squared. The active normalization instead gives norm(M) squared at most M_max; hence bar u squared is at most M_max times the deviation norm squared, and only then does the constant-vector norm produce the single L_v factor used in gamma_h.
issues.overall_effect: The stated value of gamma_h is not derived by the old proof, leaving prop:coercivity and its use in thm:main_AP unsupported at that constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the normalization Σ_q M_qΔv=1 to obtain ||M||_v²=Σ_q M_q²Δv≤M_max. Then |bar u|²≤M_max||u-bar u||_v² and ||bar u||_v²=L_v|bar u|², which gives the stated factor (1+√(L_vM_max))². The existing γ_h and its use in thm:main_AP can then be retained.
issues.why_classification: The old transition drops an additional factor of L_v and is a genuine invalid estimate. A one-line normalization and Cauchy–Schwarz correction already supported by the source restores exactly the claimed constant and dependent bounds, with no nontrivial lemma or mathematical loss.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: \|M\|_{v}^{h,2} = \sum_q M_q^2 \Delta v \le M_{\max}\sum_q M_q \Delta v = M_{\max}

issues.title: Incorrect tensor-factor decomposition in the projection bound
issues.failure_explanation: Both old difference operators annihilate a velocity-constant vector, whereas the two beta-grouped parts of eq:fp_discrete_separable generally do not. Expanding the old tensor sum also produces extra beta-weighted and beta^{-1}-weighted neighbor and diagonal terms absent from the stencil. Consequently, the asserted tensor identity is false and the subsequent norm estimates concern different operators from the actual Fokker--Planck operator.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:fluctuation_bound does not establish its kappa_h estimate for the actual operator, so the orthogonal-component estimate used by thm:main_AP is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Regroup the actual stencil as L_h=β⊗T^(α)+β^{-1}⊗T^(1/α), with T^(α)w_q=Δv^{-2}(α_{q+1/2}w_{q+1}-α_{q-1/2}w_q) and T^(1/α)w_q=Δv^{-2}(α_{q-1/2}^{-1}w_{q-1}-α_{q+1/2}^{-1}w_q). Since these velocity maps preserve ran(P_X), repeat the spatial fluctuation subtraction and apply the routine bounds ||T^(α)||≤2α_max/Δv² and ||T^(1/α)||≤2/(α_minΔv²). This recovers the same κ_h and the same use in thm:main_AP.
issues.why_classification: The displayed tensor identity is false, so the issue is substantive rather than a typo. However, the complete correction is a direct local collection of terms from the already stated stencil followed by elementary shift-and-diagonal norm estimates; it requires no new proof architecture and preserves the proposition and downstream theorem exactly.

issues.title: Half-grid maximum is insufficient in the AP theorem
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem defines M_max^{n+1} using only M_{p,q+1/2}^{n+1}, but its proof uses that quantity to bound the cell-centered factors in rho M and g=M(g/M). From eq:flux_half_def, a strict cell-centered Maxwellian maximum can exceed each adjacent geometric mean; for example, an interior grid point aligned with the Maxwellian center is larger than its neighboring half-grid values. Thus the proof supports the theorem only with a cell-centered, or combined cell/half-grid, maximum.
issues.overall_effect: The absorption condition and the constants in both bounds of thm:main_AP are not established for every field satisfying the old half-grid-only condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define M_max^{n+1}:=max{max_{p,q}M_{p,q}^{n+1}, max_{p,q}M_{p,q+1/2}^{n+1}} and use this combined maximum consistently in the small-fluctuation condition, Θ, the state-norm estimate, and both conclusions of thm:main_AP.
issues.why_classification: The half-grid maximum cannot provide the centered bounds used in the proof. Enlarging it to the combined grid maximum is a routine local norm-bound qualification: it may slightly strengthen the technical small-fluctuation condition but leaves the method, model class, conclusion, and AP rate unchanged in the intended regular regime.

issues.title: Wrong advection sign in the projected residual
issues.failure_explanation: For the actual L-step, time difference equals projected advection plus epsilon^{-1} times the projected collision operator. Solving this equation for the collision operator gives epsilon times the time difference minus projected advection. The old proof instead starts from a false negative-advection version of the update and obtains a plus sign, so its key identity and the estimate epsilon times the norm of G do not apply to the defined scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of both residual and distance bounds in thm:main_AP analyzes a different signed update from the actual first-order algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the actual projected L-step equation (f^{n+1}-f^{(2)})/Δt=P_X^{n+1}A_h(f^{(2)})+ε^{-1}P_X^{n+1}L_h^{n+1}(f^{n+1}), and consequently define G^{n+1}=(f^{n+1}-f^{(2)})/Δt-P_X^{n+1}A_h(f^{(2)}). The remaining decomposition, norm estimates, and both theorem bounds then apply unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Although the correct sign is uniquely fixed by the algorithm, the old proof's key identity and its residual G use the opposite sign and therefore literally analyze a different update; an algebraic inference must be repaired, so the narrow typo test is not met. Propagating the corrected sign is nonetheless a short local repair that preserves every substantive guarantee and rate.
